title: Mahavira
summary: Mahavira is the Jain teacher said by tradition to have been born around 599 BCE at Kundagrama in Bihar to a warrior-clan family. By thirty he had renounced his position, spent twelve years in hardship and meditation, reached omniscience and then taught a community of monks, nuns and laity. Modern scholars date his life 539–467 BCE, and his birth and death places are disputed.

uncertainty.note: Start and end follow Jain tradition (c. 599-527 BCE per World History Encyclopedia; EBSCO gives only around 599 BCE). The page also gives a modern scholarly consensus of 539-467 BCE, so the plus range reaches -538 and -466.

where.modern_name: Vaishali district, Bihar, India (area pin for Kundagrama, named by EBSCO as his birthplace in Bihar; exact site and death place are disputed)
where.historical_name: Kundagrama in Magadha, per EBSCO; his mother was sister of the king of Vaishali

importance.justification: Central teacher of the Jain tradition who organized the community of monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, per EBSCO.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Vaishali district

reviewer_note: Life details rest on Jain literature and are tradition, not independently documented; the sects differ on marriage and clothing. World History Encyclopedia says place of birth and death are disputed. Pin is a district centroid, not a site. I took the queue entry (year -599, religion) to mean the Jain teacher, not the ninth-century mathematician Mahavira.
